news.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: Portugal star breaks silence over national team walkout in statement
news.lede: Cristiano Ronaldo has broken his silence over his Portugal walkout in a lengthy statement in which he says he is not retiring from the national team. The 41-year-old, whose actions had raised doubts over his international future, accused Portugal's new head coach Jorge Jesus of broken promises in a near 2,000-word statement to his 679 million Instagram followers. You can read the statement in full at the bottom of this article. Addressing the uncertainty over his Portugal future, the Al Nassr forward said: "If I am physically well, playing for my club, with goals I hope, after serving the suspension that may be applied to me, I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team."

news.title: Women's World Cup 2027: How can England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland qualify?
news.lede: The 10th Fifa Women's World Cup will take place in Brazil between 24 June and 25 July 2027. England must get through two rounds of home and away ties to qualify for the Women's World Cup in Brazil. Sarina Wiegman's European champions will play Greece in Crete in round one of the play-offs, with the first leg on Friday, 9 October at 17:30 BST. The second leg will be played at home, at King Power Stadium in Leicester, on Tuesday, 13 October at 19:30 BST.

news.title: Warrington football star Jarell Quansah determined to learn from World Cup red card
news.lede: THINGS are on the up again for Warrington football star Jarell Quansah. He has far worse memories of England’s famous World Cup win in Mexico than most, with the red-carded defender determined to learn from his “horrible” evening at the Azteca. The versatile 23-year-old started at right-back against the co-hosts in July’s pulsating last-16 tie, but his match came to a premature end when he was sent off early in the second half following a VAR review. Quansah’s clumsy tackle meant he nervously had to watch Thomas Tuchel’s men hang on for a memorable 3-2 win from the dressing room, with FIFA’s surprising two-match ban only compounding the hurt.

news.title: Women's Football | Romania's national team will face Norway in the first round of the playoff for the World Cup
news.lede: Romania's women's national football team will face Norway in the first round of the play-off for qualification for the 2027 World Cup. The first leg is scheduled for Friday, October 9, at 20:00, at the “Arcul de Triumf” Stadium in Bucharest, while the return leg will be played on Tuesday, October 13, at 19:00, at Ullevaal Stadion in Oslo. The winner of the first round will play against the winner of the Albania – Wales tie. The second play-off round will be played at the end of November and beginning of December.

news.title: COSAFA Member Association presidents join African football leaders at Caf Strategy Conference
news.lede: Presidents from COSAFA’s Member Associations will be among the leading football decision-makers attending the landmark CAF Strategy Conference in Santa Maria, Sal Island, Cabo Verde, which runs from October 7-9. The three-day gathering, convened under the leadership of CAF President Dr Patrice Motsepe, brings together the Presidents of CAF’s 54 Member Associations, Zonal Union Presidents, CAF Executive Committee members, National Team coaches, technical leaders and international football experts. FIFA President Gianni Infantino is also attending the Conference. Thursday’s programme includes the CAF Member Associations’ Strategy Meeting, where COSAFA’s football leadership will join colleagues from across the continent to discuss the future direction of the African game.

news.title: Counter-Pressing Defined the 2026 World Cup: What FIFA’s Technical Report Tells Coaches
news.lede: FIFA has published its post-tournament technical report on the 2026 World Cup, and its headline finding will shape coaching conversations for years: counter-pressing, the instant hunt for the ball in the seconds after losing it, was the tournament’s defining tactical trend. The report, compiled by FIFA’s Technical Study Group and the Football Performance Insights Department from all 104 matches and released on 3 October, concluded that champions Spain were its finest exponents, using their in-possession structure to regain the ball before opponents could reorganise. The report is the work of the Technical Study Group (TSG) and FIFA’s Football Performance Insights Department, who studied every one of the 104 matches with data, tracking and video.

news.title: Messi’s farewell, Ronaldo’s exile, Bangladesh’s ASEAN Cup woes: Events aplenty in football’s longest window
news.lede: The curtain has officially fallen on the longest international break in FIFA history, a marathon three-week window that disrupted club calendars, stretched national-team squad depths to their limits, and delivered some of the most dramatic storylines the sport has seen. From tearful goodbyes in Buenos Aires and tactical mutinies in Lisbon to historic South Asian showdowns and new superstars stepping into the spotlight, this international break offered no shortage of talking points. Here is a breakdown of the biggest moments, heartbreaks and triumphs that defined the window:. Messi’s emotional international retirement.
